notice: Simulated three-year guide; real local engine output, not market prices or forecasts.
introduction: New to moving averages and upward crossing buy signals?
recovery: An SMA smooths recent closing prices. An upward crossing occurs when price moves from below the SMA to above it. Some investors use it as a buy signal because it may suggest that the price is beginning to recover. Waiting for a crossing can filter out some buys while price is still below its average.
risk: It does not guarantee a recovery or stop an investment falling after a buy. SMAs lag prices, and false crossings can be followed by renewed declines. This three-year simulated chart deliberately includes reversals as well as recoveries.
comparison: Choose a crossing frequency to see its SMA and investment-return comparisons. The optimizer matches crossing frequency, not profit. The comparisons use $100 per buy: a. upward crossings; b. equal-period buys; c. the most common of 500 random-buy scenarios, with the same number of buys in each. These are simulations, not forecasts.
